name: Vaginal steaming and herbal feminine cleansing
what_people_do: Sit over herbal steam or use herbal washes to "clean" the womb after periods or birth; promoted through wellness networks.
why_they_say_it_works: To detox the womb, ease cramps, restore the vagina after birth or treat infection.

documented_by.source: Black women's perceptions of vaginal steaming in the USA, 2026, Cult Health Sex, PMID 41618892
documented_by.quote_or_summary: US interview study, 8 Black women aged 23 to 70: only one had tried vaginal steaming; others were wary of safety, cost and medical credibility; information spread through interpersonal and digital networks.

documented_by.source: Vardeman ET, Kennelly EJ, Vandebroek I 2024, J Ethnobiol Ethnomed, PMID 38217006
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Haitian women in NYC: vaginal cleansing was a priority concern treated with plants.

evidence.finding: No trial in the studies I read; my PubMed survey search for vaginal steaming returned nothing relevant before the 2026 interview paper.

source.name: agent4-traditional-practices.md, 12 Nov 2026 (research file in this project)

harm_note: Framed as medically risky in the paper; Caribbean ethnobotany authors hypothesise microbiome disruption. No injury data opened.
gaps: No injury or infection figures; West African steaming not documented by an opened survey.
